title: Transport survey
transcript:
Speaker 0: Part one. You will hear an interview with a woman who is doing a survey on transport. First, you have some time to look at questions one to five. Now listen carefully and answer questions one to five.
Speaker 1: Excuse me. Would you mind if I asked you some questions? We're doing a survey on transport.
Speaker 2: Yes. That's okay.
Speaker 1: First of all, can I take your name?
Speaker 2: Yes. It's Sadie Jones.
Speaker 1: Thanks very much. And could I have your date of birth? Just the year will do, actually. Is that alright?
Speaker 2: Yes. That's fine. It's 1991.
Speaker 1: So next, your postcode, please.
Speaker 2: It's DW37YZed.
Speaker 1: Great. Thanks. Is that in Wells?
Speaker 2: No. It's actually in Harbourn. Wells isn't far from there, though.
Speaker 1: I really like that area. My grandmother lived there when I was a kid.
Speaker 2: Yes. It is nice.
Speaker 1: Right. So now I want to ask you some questions about how you traveled here today. Did you use public transport?
Speaker 2: Yes. I came by bus.
Speaker 1: Okay. And that was today. It's the April 24, isn't it?
Speaker 2: Isn't it the twenty fifth? No. Actually, you're right.
Speaker 1: And what was the reason for your trip today? I can see you've got some shopping with you.
Speaker 2: Yes. I did some shopping. But the main reason I came here was to go to the dentist.
Speaker 1: That's not much fun. Hope it was nothing serious.
Speaker 2: No. It was just a checkup. It's fine.
Speaker 1: Good. Do you normally travel by bus into the city center?
Speaker 2: Yes. I stopped driving in ages ago because parking was so difficult to find, and it costs so much.
Speaker 1: I see.
Speaker 2: The bus is much more convenient too. It only takes about thirty minutes.
Speaker 1: That's good. So where did you start your journey?
Speaker 2: At the bus stop on Claxby Street.
Speaker 1: Is that C L A X B Y?
Speaker 2: That's right.
Speaker 0: Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions six to 10. Now listen and answer questions six to 10.
Speaker 1: And how satisfied with the service are you? Do you have any complaints?
Speaker 2: Well, as I said, it's very convenient and quick when it's on time. But this morning, it was late. Only about ten minutes, but still
Speaker 1: Yes. I understand that's annoying. And what about the timetable? Do you have any comments about that?
Speaker 2: I suppose I mainly use the bus during the day. But anytime I've been in town in the evening, for dinner or at the cinema, I've noticed you have to wait a long time for a bus. There aren't that many.
Speaker 1: Okay. Thanks. So now I'd like to ask you about your car use.
Speaker 2: Well, I have got a car, but I don't use it that often, mainly just to go to the supermarket. But that's about it, really. My husband uses it at the weekends to go to the golf club.
Speaker 1: And what about a bicycle?
Speaker 2: I don't actually have one at the moment.
Speaker 1: What about the Citi Bikes you can rent? Do you ever use those?
Speaker 2: No. I'm not keen on cycling there because of all the pollution. But I would like to get a bike. It would be good to use it to get to work.
Speaker 1: So why haven't you got one now?
Speaker 2: Well, I live in a flat on the 2nd Floor, and it doesn't have any storage. So we'd have to leave it in the hall outside the flat.
Speaker 1: I see. Okay. Well, I think that's all we need from you today, say
Speaker 0: That is the end of part one. You now have one minute to check your answers to part one. Part two. You will hear a woman speaking to a group of people who are interested in becoming volunteers for an organization called ACE. First, you have some time to look at questions 11 to 15.
